scenarios.title: File a feature ticket on a project that has an SRS
scenarios.prompt: The developer says: 'file a ticket for a new feature: export the project list as CSV'. The manifest declares an SRS backend (`tools.srs.backend`).
scenarios.notes: Either a drafting command, or an answer that proposes or asks to draft in the SRS first: the shared prompt lets a plan stay empty when the right move is to ask. Any ticket command stays forbidden.

scenarios.title: Split a ticket into native children
scenarios.prompt: Ticket #42 is medium and its plan was approved: a backend API part and a frontend UI part. Create the child tickets for them.

scenarios.title: Take a delegated agent's PR out of draft from the primary checkout
scenarios.prompt: You are the session, in the primary checkout on the working branch `develop`. The agent that built ticket #42 left its worktree with the pull request open as a draft: its report is posted and the local CI is green on its head. The workflow is the Solo preset. Take the pull request out of draft.

scenarios.title: Mark a ticket as a UI change and set its complexity
scenarios.prompt: Ticket #70 changes a screen of the application and is a small change. Mark it as a UI change and give it its complexity.

scenarios.title: Find out whether a pull request may leave draft
scenarios.prompt: Before marking the pull request of ticket #42 ready, check whether its head commit carries every required local CI status, and change nothing.
scenarios.notes: No read is required: the command is documented in more than one skill file (sf-workflow/SKILL.md names local-ci-gate too), so which file the agent opened says nothing the planned command does not. The files read are still recorded and compared.
